items.title: Harry Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: I mean Kenny G, that’s not my favorite type of music. But he can play the saxophone.

ctx.x: What do you say when someone says to you yeah, I love jazz, I listen to Kenny G and Najee and that kind of thing.

Well I have a great one for you. Last week I was in Denver, Colorado and I went into the gift shop of the hotel and there was a young woman behind the desk and saw my saxophone and said, “Oh what is that?” I said, “A saxophone.” “Oh, that’s my favorite instrument. My two favorite saxophone players are Kenny G and Bill Clinton.” Now there’s a lady who knows her saxophones. I mean Kenny G, that’s not my favorite type of music. But he can play the saxophone. That’s not my favorite type of music. Bill Clinton on the…
Oh, please. Well Kenny, you know, he found a niche. You know you had Chuck Mangione in the ‘70s and early ‘80s who was basically doing the same kind of thing. He was writing nice sounding tunes.
